bib.title: Large Language Models can Learn Rules

read.skipped: Appendix B prompts 4-15 and C rule libraries skimmed by heading only (long prompt listings); all else read.

question: Can an LLM learn an explicit library of textual rules from training examples without rule annotation, and does prompting with that library beat relying on the model's implicit rules?
hypothesis: Incorrect implicit rules cause many CoT errors; retrieving verified rules from a learned library is easier than generating them, so reasoning improves.
contributions: Hypotheses-to-Theories (HtT): induction stage that generates and verifies rules, deduction stage that applies a filtered rule library
Induction from deduction: reuse one few-shot deductive prompt (CoT, LtM) for rule generation and verification
XML tagging of a hierarchical rule library to make retrieval work in a pure-prompting setup
10-30% absolute accuracy gains on CLUTRR, Arithmetic and List Functions; rules transfer across models and to textual CLUTRR

method.summary: Induction stage: run few-shot CoT/LtM on training QA pairs, extract each declared rule by regex, count occurrences and correct answers per rule, keep rules with coverage >= k and confidence >= p. Deduction stage: prepend the rule library (organised under XML tags) to the few-shot prompt, with exemplars teaching the model to retrieve rules rather than generate them.
method.task: multi-step reasoning with prompting: relational reasoning (CLUTRR), non-decimal arithmetic, concept learning (List Functions)

datasets.name: CLUTRR (symbolic and textual)
datasets.size: train 2,000 samples of 2 and 3 hop; validation 200 and test 200 samples of 2 to 10 hop
datasets.split: uniform sampling of standard splits from Sinha et al. 2019
datasets.preprocessing: rules induced on symbolic version; textual version reuses them

datasets.name: Arithmetic (Wu et al. 2023), bases 16, 11, 9
datasets.size: train 900 examples of 2-digit addition; validation 100 and test 100 examples of 2, 3 and 4 digit addition
datasets.preprocessing: when the training set has fewer than 2,000 examples, resampled up to 2,000 for induction

datasets.name: List Functions
datasets.size: 250 tasks (P1, P2, P3), 32 input-output pairs per task
datasets.split: 16 train, 16 test per task; for HtT the 16 train split into 8 train and 8 validation
datasets.preprocessing: induction run on 20 train-validation splits sampled per task

other.note: reproduced by authors in the same setting, CLUTRR only

inference.decoding: sampling; no other decoding settings stated
inference.temperature: 1 (default) for GPT-3.5 and GPT-4; 0.9 for Gemini Pro
inference.samples: inferred: one run per item; number of runs and seeds not stated
inference.prompting: 0-shot CoT; 5-shot CoT and 5-shot LtM (first 5 non-trivial examples) on CLUTRR and Arithmetic; 4-shot CoT (first example of each of 4 groups in P1) on List Functions; same exemplars across methods; HtT prepends the rule library and an instruction to use the provided knowledge
inference.retrieval: no external retriever: the LLM retrieves rules itself from the library in the prompt, indexed via XML tags (2 levels for CLUTRR, 3 for Arithmetic)

parameters.induction training examples: 2,000 for CLUTRR and Arithmetic; 20 train-val splits per List Functions task
parameters.rule library size limit: <= 500 rules in experiments; base method needs >= 20% training accuracy

other.LtM rule induction: hyperparameters selected and rules induced with CoT; LtM used only for deduction
other.answer matching: last sentence of output, full-word match; multiple answers count as wrong

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: ground-truth answer appears as full word in last sentence of the prediction

metrics.name: task accuracy (List Functions)
metrics.definition: ratio of tasks with all test pairs solved

eval.protocol: no seeds, variance or significance tests stated; test sets are small (200 CLUTRR, 100 per Arithmetic base/digit set); manual error analysis on 100 test examples

prompts.text: Instruction: When you answer the questions, try to use the provided knowledge whenever possible. Try not to invent knowledge by yourself unless necessary.
Context: The relations on the path from {{ head }} to {{ tail }} are {{ relations[0] }}, . . . , {{ relations[n - 1] }}. Question: {{ tail }} is {{ head }}'s what? Answer: Let's think step by step.

limits: Authors: needs a base model with reasonably strong knowledge and retrieval; GPT-3.5 gains are marginal on Arithmetic (Table 2) and textual CLUTRR (+0.3).
Authors: number of rules is limited by the LLM context length; scaling beyond the context is open.
Rule library hierarchy for XML tags is defined manually.
Only applicable to tasks with <= 500 rules and >= 20% base accuracy on training examples; excludes planning tasks.
Authors cannot guarantee numbers reproduce on future model versions (GPT-3.5/GPT-4 updated).
LtM hyperparameters chosen from CoT, which may underestimate LtM+HtT.
No variance, seeds or significance tests stated; test sets small (200 CLUTRR, 100 per Arithmetic cell).
Only gpt-3.5-turbo-0613, gpt-4-0613 and gemini-1.0-pro; models are dated.
CLUTRR rules are not deterministic (a grandmother's daughter can be mother or aunt) so recall of rules can only be checked on Arithmetic.

terms.definition: a framework that learns a rule library for reasoning with LLMs, in an induction stage and a deduction stage
adapts a deductive reasoning prompt (e.g. CoT, LtM) for both rule generation and verification by explicitly declaring a rule whenever a deduction is performed
coverage = number of occurrences of a rule in the training set; confidence = average accuracy of examples where the rule occurs
